headline: Approved a dimensional variance and special use permit for a 288-square-foot shed at 45 Oakdale Avenue, 5-0.
summary: The board heard one appeal from Edward R. Laplume for a 288-square-foot shed at 45 Oakdale Avenue, where a 150-square-foot shed is allowed. Members voted 5-0 to approve the dimensional variance and special use permit, with a special condition to repair the shed as needed.

APPEAL NO. 1: Edward R. Laplume, applicant and owner of the property at 45 Oakdale Avenue,
further identified as Tax Assessor's Plat 48 Lot 635, located in an "RT" Residential Two-Family Zone, is
requesting a Dimensional Variance under Section 410-46 and a Special Use Permit under Section
410-12.2(C) of the Pawtucket Zoning Ordinance.  The applicant is proposing to place a 288-square-foot
shed on the property where a 150-square-foot shed is allowed.
The objectors were heard on October 26, 2026.

FINDINGS:
The subject property consists of Lot 635, containing approximately 7,682 square feet of land, and is
improved with a single-family dwelling.  The applicant purchased the property in August 2026 and
subsequently placed a 12-foot by 24-foot accessory storage shed, containing approximately 288
square feet, on the premises.
The hardship associated with the requested dimensional variance results from a prior action taken by
the applicant, who installed the accessory storage shed after purchasing the property.
Although the hardship is self-created, Rhode Island General Laws § 45-24-41 provides that the fact
that a hardship is self-created does not, by itself, constitute grounds for denial of a dimensional
variance.
The requested dimensional variance will not alter the general character of the surrounding area or
impair the intent or purpose of the City's Zoning Ordinance or Comprehensive Plan.
Several accessory storage sheds of comparable size are located within approximately 200 feet of the
subject property.  Accordingly, the proposed accessory structure is consistent with the established
residential character of the neighborhood.
The requested relief generally conforms to the objectives of the City of Pawtucket's Comprehensive
Plan.
Section 410-12.2(C) of the City of Pawtucket's Zoning Ordinance identifies accessory storage sheds
exceeding 150 square feet as requiring a special use permit.
However, the ordinance does not appear to establish specific and objective criteria governing the
issuance of a special use permit for this particular category of accessory structure.
Rhode Island General Laws § 45-24-42(c) provides that where a zoning ordinance does not expressly
establish specific and objective criteria for the issuance of a particular category of special use permit,
that category shall be deemed a permitted use.
Accordingly, provided that no other applicable provisions of the Zoning Ordinance establish the
required criteria, the proposed accessory storage shed shall be treated as a permitted use pursuant to
state law.
This determination does not eliminate the requirement to obtain any necessary dimensional relief.
The accessory storage shed is compatible with neighboring residential land uses.  Several large
accessory storage sheds are located within approximately 200 feet of the subject property.
Page 3 of 3
October 26, 2026- Board of Appeals Hearing and Voting Meeting
The proposed structure is consistent with the existing pattern of accessory residential development
and will not substantially alter the character of the surrounding neighborhood.
Based upon the testimony and evidence presented by the applicant at the public hearing, together
with my personal inspection of the subject property, I find that denial of the requested dimensional
variance would result in an adverse impact amounting to more than a mere inconvenience.
Although the hardship results from a prior action of the applicant, this circumstance does not
automatically preclude the granting of dimensional relief.
Accessory storage sheds are customary improvements associated with single-family residential
properties, and several comparable structures exist within approximately 200 feet of the subject
property.
Accordingly, I find that the applicant has satisfied the dimensional variance hardship standard
established under Rhode Island General Laws §45-24-41(e)(2), and I support granting the requested
dimensional variance.
SPECIAL CONDITIONS:
  
Repair the shed as needed.
